positions.name: ReviewerEnrollmentAssertion
positions.frame: what warrants the claim that saving a memory enrolls its creator as a reviewer, and what standing does this document have relative to that claim?
positions.why: Both segments are read through the same relational move: an automated arbiter (the e2e suite) is granted authority to assign a social role (reviewer) as a consequence of an action (saving a memory), and the second segment explicitly frames the whole document as existing only to carry that first assertion — a self-referential vehicle for it. There is a conviction gradient worth holding in tension rather than resolving: src-1 performs a ratifying 'Decision:' speech act (settling a rule), while src-2 is a flat, unhedged claim of purpose with no ratification language — descriptive of the document's function, not itself a further ruling. Register also shifts from technical/native pipeline jargon (src-1) to plain matter-of-fact self-description (src-2), but both stay anchored in present, realis, concrete framing of the same specific artifact and rule.

placements.title: creating a memory installs its author as its reviewer
placements.frame: What does the system guarantee about who reviews a memory when its creator is the one who saved it, and under what conditions (if any) does that automatic reviewer enrollment get tested, overridden, or extended?
placements.why: src-1 states, as a settled 'Decision,' the e2e-tested rule that saving a memory enrolls its creator as a reviewer — a system behavior about how authorship confers review responsibility, the kind of policy future envelopes about review workflows, reviewer assignment, or memory lifecycle would keep feeding. src-2 doesn't add new content; it explicitly frames this whole probe document as existing solely to carry that same assertion, reinforcing rather than diluting the theme. The graph and strata are both empty for this repo, so nothing existing plausibly holds this subject — it names a recurring policy theme, not a one-time fact, so it clears the narrative grain test for a mint rather than being folded as evidence under something else.
